deck.headline: FAA halts all US departures as air traffic control communications fail nationwide
deck.sub: The third nationwide ground stop in FAA history; DHS sees no attack, and early reporting points to a bad network update.
deck.summary: The FAA halted all US departures on Friday after communication failures hit its en-route air traffic control centres. DHS says there is no sign of an attack; CBS sources say an update to ATC's private network made it reboot and crash. Thousands of flights were cancelled and more than 10,000 delayed. The full cause is not yet confirmed.
deck.whyItMatters: A single network change grounded the world's busiest airspace for hours, a day after a Microsoft 365 outage traced to a network capacity upgrade. Banks and insurers should expect claims, travel-cover and business-interruption questions, and every operations team should re-read its own change-control rules for shared networks.
deck.checked: Checked on the FAA's own statement; cause, counts and quotes from ABC News, Ars Technica and Business Insider
deck.storyline: Storyline: when air traffic systems fail · day 1
deck.detailHtml:
The FAA issued a nationwide ground stop for all US airports on Friday afternoon, citing communication issues affecting multiple Air Route Traffic Control Centers, the 22 centres that handle planes above 18,000 feet. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin called it a telecommunications outage with no indication of a "nefarious" act. Multiple sources told CBS News an update to the private network that links the air traffic control system made it reboot and crash. By the evening FlightAware counted more than 4,000 cancellations and 10,000+ delays (ABC); some flights were later allowed to depart as centres recovered. Ars Technica says it is only the third nationwide ground stop in FAA history. The contractor behind the FAA's new AI congestion tool, and Microsoft, both said they were not the cause (Business Insider).

The FAA's statement is brief and marked preliminary: a nationwide ground stop for all US airports following communication issues at multiple Air Route Traffic Control Centers, with technicians investigating. Everything about the cause comes from reporting. CBS News, citing multiple sources, says an update to the private communications network connecting the air traffic control system caused it to reboot and crash. Bloomberg reports the FBI is looking at whether a bad software update was responsible. DHS says there is no sign of an attack.

The impact landed on a Friday evening: thousands of cancellations, college sports teams stranded, Canadian airports bracing for knock-on delays. The FAA said some flights could depart as en-route centres recovered, but no all-clear had been given at the time of writing.

deck.headline: ChatGPT Wallet lets OpenAI's agents pay with your card, without seeing it
deck.summary: OpenAI launched ChatGPT Wallet, letting its dots agents buy things for a limited group of US Pro users with Visa, Mastercard or Amex cards. Agents pay with a network token, never the card number, and each purchase needs Face ID or a fingerprint. OpenAI takes no transaction cut at launch and plans spending limits and category rules.
deck.whyItMatters: This is the card networks' tokenised agent-payment rails going live inside the biggest consumer AI app. Issuers need to decide how their fraud models treat agent-initiated, biometrically approved transactions, who is liable when an agent buys the wrong thing, and how disputes will work.
deck.checked: Checked on TechCrunch's report of the launch; OpenAI's own post blocked automated access (403)
deck.storyline: Storyline: AI agents that buy things · day 18
deck.detailHtml: OpenAI launched ChatGPT Wallet, which lets its dots agents choose and complete purchases. It starts with a limited number of US ChatGPT Pro subscribers aged 18+ with a US-issued Visa, Mastercard or American Express card. The agent pays with a payment token rather than the card number, users review the items, total and card first, and every purchase is approved with Face ID or a fingerprint, keeping existing card rewards and protections. OpenAI plans spending limits and rules by category or time window so agents can be pre-approved; CNBC reports OpenAI is not taking a share of transaction revenue at launch. OpenAI warns some sites and fraud systems will still block agent purchases.

deck.headline: Ten-year yield hits 5.17% as December hike bets grow; bitcoin breaks $70,000
deck.summary: The US 10-year Treasury yield touched 5.17% on Friday, its highest since October, as traders priced a December Fed hike. The Nasdaq fell about 0.9% as Nvidia's slide deepened, the Dow edged up, and bitcoin dropped below $70,000 for the first time in nearly three months. Exact closing yields vary by source, around 5.13%.
deck.whyItMatters: A 5%+ 10-year resets mortgage, corporate-bond and bank funding costs, and puts pressure on bond portfolios held at fair value. With a December hike now the base case for many traders, treasury desks should stress-test deposit costs and unrealised losses again.

deck.storyline: Storyline: where interest rates go · day 4

deck.headline: Nvidia sounds out Arm's Rene Haas as Reuters says Huang misled his lawyer
deck.summary: Nvidia's board has approached Arm CEO Rene Haas about the top job, the FT reports, though the board says it has not formally engaged candidates. Reuters says Jensen Huang misled Nvidia's general counsel about his relationship with Alice Huang. Staff are petitioning for his return, and Malaysia and Singapore have stepped up chip-smuggling probes.
deck.whyItMatters: The governance story is widening into a compliance one: misleading the general counsel and new export probes raise legal risk for Nvidia and for anyone in its distribution chain. The CEO pick, and whether it is an outsider, will set the tone for China policy talks next week.
deck.update: Nvidia's board reportedly approached Arm CEO Rene Haas; Reuters says Huang misled Nvidia's general counsel about the affair; staff petition for his return; Malaysia and Singapore step up chip probes.
deck.storyline: Storyline: who runs Nvidia · day 2
deck.detailHtml: Nvidia's board has approached Arm CEO Rene Haas, a former Nvidia executive, about succeeding Jensen Huang, the FT reports; the board says it is still choosing a search firm and has not formally engaged candidates. Reuters reports Huang misled general counsel Tim Teter and CMO Alison Wagonfeld in October about his relationship with Megaspeed's Alice Huang, calling it normal business dealings. An internal post urging the board to weigh staff views drew hundreds of comments calling for Huang's return (Hacker News thread: 789 points). Malaysia is investigating whether hardware imported by a Megaspeed subsidiary was re-exported, and Singapore has charged another executive over 917 servers that may contain Nvidia GPUs (Tom's Hardware).

deck.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin to meet together in Shenzhen on 19 November
deck.summary: The White House says Trump will meet Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin together on 19 November in Shenzhen, on the sidelines of APEC: the first such three-way meeting. Nuclear arms reduction and the Iran war are expected topics; Ukraine largely is not. US officials say they do not expect an agreement.
deck.whyItMatters: The meeting lands the same week as Nvidia's leadership crisis and pending US chip curbs, so any word on export controls or AI dialogue will move chip and China-exposed stocks. Expect volatility in oil if Iran comes up.
deck.storyline: Storyline: the Trump, Xi and Putin summit · day 1
deck.detailHtml: The leaders of the US, China and Russia plan to meet on Thursday 19 November on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, the White House says, an unprecedented gathering of the heads of the world's largest nuclear powers. AP reports nuclear arms reduction will be discussed and Trump is expected to raise the Iran war, while a US official said he will steer away from Ukraine. Analysts expect symbolism over substance and US officials do not expect an agreement.

deck.headline: RBI clears Paytm to restart wallets through a new subsidiary, in principle
deck.summary: The RBI has given Paytm Payments Services, a subsidiary of Paytm's parent, in-principle approval to issue wallets and other prepaid instruments, years after its payments bank was shut down. It must pass a system and cybersecurity audit within six months before it can launch. Paytm shares hit a record high.
deck.whyItMatters: The RBI is letting a once-sanctioned group back into wallets through a cleaner structure, which tells fintechs how to rebuild after enforcement. Banks competing for UPI and wallet users should expect Paytm to push hard once final approval comes.
deck.storyline: Storyline: India's payment licences · day 1
deck.detailHtml: The Reserve Bank of India has granted Paytm Payments Services Ltd (PPSL), a wholly owned subsidiary of One 97 Communications, in-principle authorisation to issue and operate prepaid payment instruments, including wallets. PPSL must complete a system and cybersecurity audit within six months or the approval lapses, and can issue wallets only after final authorisation. Paytm's old wallet ran through Paytm Payments Bank, which the RBI barred from new customers in 2022 and from new deposits in 2024; this approval is for a separate entity. Paytm shares hit a record high.

deck.headline: Trump names four SEC and CFTC picks, including Hester Peirce's successor
deck.summary: Trump nominated Steven Levine to replace crypto advocate Hester Peirce at the SEC, and former CFTC commissioner Kristin Johnson for a second SEC seat. Nathan Anonick and Matthew Rowland, both Clarity Act veterans, were named to the CFTC, which has only its chairman. Confirmation must come before Democrats take the Senate in January.
deck.whyItMatters: The agencies writing US crypto and prediction-market rules have been running with skeleton commissions. Whether these nominees are confirmed this year decides how fast stablecoin, custody and event-contract rules move in 2027.
deck.storyline: Storyline: who runs US crypto regulation · day 1
deck.detailHtml: The White House nominated Steven Levine (R) for the SEC seat of Hester Peirce, who led the agency's crypto task force, and former CFTC commissioner Kristin Johnson (D) for Caroline Crenshaw's seat. At the CFTC, where chairman Mike Selig is the sole commissioner, it nominated Nathan Anonick (R) and Matthew Rowland (D), both of whom worked on the Clarity Act. Levine's views on crypto are less publicly known; Johnson has pushed for stronger customer protection. Republicans have only a short lame-duck window before Democrats take the Senate in January.
deck.sourcesHtml: REPORTINGCointelegraphAGGREGATORMLQ.ai

deck.headline: Trezor finds phrase-stealing implants in three hardware wallets from one reseller
deck.summary: Trezor confirmed malicious hardware implants in three Safe 5 wallets sold by reseller CryptoBilis; they send recovery phrases out over a cellular link. Firmware 2.13.1 blocks the implants it found, but owners must move funds to a new seed. Trezor has cut its reseller network by about 80%. No losses have been reported, Trezor says.
deck.whyItMatters: Hardware supply chains are now an attack path for self-custody. Banks building crypto custody should buy devices only from manufacturers or audited channels and treat any third-party reseller as untrusted.
deck.storyline: Storyline: crypto theft and recovery · day 2
deck.detailHtml: Hardware-wallet maker Trezor confirmed that three Safe 5 devices sold by Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis contained malicious hardware implants that capture recovery phrases and passphrases and send them over cellular networks. The firmware and secure chip were not altered. Firmware 2.13.1, released 11 November, stops the implants it found from capturing anything, but cannot recall phrases already sent, so owners should move funds to a wallet with a new seed. Implants were earlier found in Ledger devices sold by the same reseller. Trezor has cut its reseller network by about 80%.
deck.sourcesHtml: REPORTINGBleepingComputerAGGREGATORCoinMarketCap Academy

deck.headline: FBI warns attackers are running the Artex AI hacking tool at machine speed
deck.summary: An FBI flash alert says attackers are using Artex, an AI penetration-testing platform, to automate reconnaissance and data theft at machine speed. Attacker-run instances mostly use Chinese models, led by DeepSeek Flash, because they are cheap and lack guardrails. Censys counts more than 1,600 exposed Artex consoles.
deck.whyItMatters: This moves AI-run intrusion from research to an official law-enforcement warning. Security teams should expect faster, wider scanning and shorter dwell times, and should block or monitor known Artex infrastructure.
deck.storyline: Storyline: AI tools that run cyberattacks · day 1
deck.detailHtml: An FBI flash alert says Artex, a penetration-testing platform that turns plain-language goals into attack commands, is being used by threat actors for reconnaissance and data exfiltration at machine speed. The FBI says attacker-run Artex instances mostly use Chinese models, with DeepSeek Flash models dominating for their cost and lack of guardrails when framed as pen testing, alongside Claude, GPT and others. Censys has found 1,600+ publicly exposed Artex consoles; archived copies and a commercial version keep it available.
deck.sourcesHtml: REPORTINGThe Record

deck.headline: Perplexity open-sources its Decider decision models, adding a 'locate' skill
deck.summary: Perplexity released Decider v1.3 and Decider Flash v1.3, decision models that return probabilities instead of prose, as open weights under Apache 2.0. The large model is a 26B fine-tune of Qwen3.8-27B. A new 'locate' skill returns the matching text with character offsets. Its 91.6% accuracy figure is Perplexity's own test.
deck.whyItMatters: A day after Google's Decision 1, the decision-model category now has a free, open-weight option banks can run on their own hardware for classification, routing and compliance checks. 'Locate' is directly useful for extracting clauses or fields with an audit trail.
deck.storyline: Storyline: new kinds of AI models · day 14
deck.detailHtml: Perplexity released Decider v1.3 and Decider Flash v1.3, decision models that return calibrated probabilities for yes/no, multiple-choice and scored questions rather than prose. The weights are on Hugging Face under Apache 2.0; the large model is a 26B fine-tune of Qwen3.8-27B per its model card, and Flash is distilled from it. New in v1.3 is locate: describe what to find and the model returns the matching text with character offsets. CEO Aravind Srinivas says both are free on OpenRouter for a week. Perplexity reports 91.6% mean accuracy on 63 internal tasks (its own benchmark).

deck.headline: OpenAI folds its robotics team into core research as GPT-6 Astra runs robots
deck.summary: OpenAI has disbanded its separate robotics team, moving researchers into core research and hardware staff into its Applied organisation, Fortune reports. OpenAI says general models such as GPT-6 Astra can already run some robot tasks directly. It still plans a first public humanoid demonstration in 2027.
deck.whyItMatters: The bet that one general model can drive robots, cars and drones is spreading. If it holds, robotics value shifts from specialised model labs to hardware, data and deployment, which matters for how investors price start-ups like Agile Robots and Figure.
deck.storyline: Storyline: AI acting in the physical world · day 19
deck.detailHtml: OpenAI has disbanded its stand-alone robotics team, Fortune reports. Robotics research moves under chief research officer Mark Chen, and applied robotics and hardware staff join the Applied organisation under president Greg Brockman. OpenAI says researchers have seen surprising results connecting GPT-6 Astra directly to robots, so separate robot-specific models may not be needed, and that it still aims for a first public humanoid demonstration in 2027. deck.headline: Claude helps surface 663 theorems hidden in Kurt Gödel's notebooks
deck.summary: A Helsinki logician gave Claude his transcriptions of Kurt Gödel's 1940s notebooks. Claude catalogued 663 theorems Gödel had proved, sketched or outlined. Checked in the Coq proof assistant, about 400 held as stated, about 200 needed repair and about 50 were false. A human read the shorthand; Claude did the analysis.
deck.whyItMatters: A good example of AI as a research accelerant on archives too large for a human: the model did the reading and cataloguing, a proof assistant checked the results, and a human expert framed the work. The same pattern fits legacy code and document archives in banks.
deck.storyline: Storyline: AI doing mathematics · day 1
deck.detailHtml: Since 2017 Jan von Plato at the University of Helsinki has studied 16 notebooks, 1,009 pages, that Kurt Gödel wrote in the early 1940s in an obsolete German shorthand, at about a page a week. In September he gave his transcriptions to Claude, which produced a digest within days showing Gödel had proved hundreds of unknown theorems. Asked to extract every theorem Gödel proved, sketched or had an idea for, Claude found 663. Checked in the Coq proof assistant, about 400 were verified as stated, about 200 needed repair and about 50 were false, the Guardian reports. Claude did not read the shorthand; von Plato did.
deck.sourcesHtml: REPORTINGThe GuardianOTHERHacker News (316 points)

deck.headline: IEA says oil is back in surplus for the first time since the Iran war
deck.summary: The IEA says oil supply has exceeded demand for the first time since the Iran war began, with inventories up about 1.7 million barrels a day in October as Gulf exports recover. It now expects a fourth-quarter surplus. North Sea crude is about $93, down from $136 in October, but diesel remains very tight.
deck.whyItMatters: Lower crude helps the inflation outlook that is pushing yields above 5%, but diesel tightness keeps freight and farm costs high. Lenders to airlines, shippers and refiners should watch the gap between crude and product prices.
deck.storyline: Storyline: the Iran war and the economy · day 4
deck.detailHtml: The International Energy Agency's November report says global oil supply has exceeded demand for the first time since the Iran war began, with crude inventories rising by about 1.7M barrels a day in October as Gulf exports recovered faster than demand, though they remain 26% below pre-war levels. The IEA now sees a fourth-quarter surplus (it had forecast a deficit) and a larger build in 2027. North Sea Dated fell about 32% from a $136 peak in early October to about $93. Diesel supply remains severely tight, at record prices in the US.

deck.headline: Microsoft blames a network upgrade bug for its two-day 365 outage, and apologises
deck.summary: Microsoft says the Microsoft 365 outage that took down Outlook, Teams and Copilot came from a bug introduced during a network capacity upgrade, not an attack. It said it was deeply sorry and that recovery was improving on day two, without a full timeline. A post-incident report will follow.
deck.whyItMatters: Two network-change failures in two days (Microsoft and the FAA) are the strongest argument yet for treating your cloud provider's change process as your own operational risk. Banks should check what their DORA and RBI outsourcing plans assume about a 24-hour productivity-suite outage.
deck.update: Microsoft blames a bug introduced during a network capacity upgrade, rules out an attack, apologises, and reports gradual recovery on day two.
deck.storyline: Storyline: when one cloud fails · day 2
deck.detailHtml: Microsoft says the outage that took down Outlook, Teams, Copilot and other Microsoft 365 services from 12 November was caused by a bug introduced during a network capacity upgrade, with no sign of a cyberattack. "We are deeply sorry for the disruption," a spokesperson said; a full post-incident report will follow. On Friday it reported service availability and email delivery improving across a growing share of infrastructure, but gave no full-recovery time. The BBC says NHS trusts, schools and police forces were hit; TechCabal says Kenyan banks moved to WhatsApp and phone lines.
deck.sourcesHtml: REPORTINGThe Spokesman-Review · Insurance Business: cloud concentration riskOTHERBBC News video: what we know

deck.headline: DOJ and CFTC sue Arkansas to shield Kalshi as Louisiana opens a new front
deck.summary: The Justice Department and CFTC sued Arkansas to stop its gambling case against Kalshi, arguing event contracts are swaps that only the CFTC regulates. Arkansas is the 11th state the CFTC has sued. Louisiana's attorney general separately sued Kalshi, Polymarket, Robinhood and Coinbase. Kalshi is reportedly in talks at a $65 billion valuation.
deck.whyItMatters: The federal government is now litigating on behalf of an industry its own regulator has threatened to charge. Banks and brokers offering event contracts face a patchwork until an appeals court or Congress settles who regulates them.
deck.update: The DOJ and CFTC sue Arkansas in federal court to stop its case against Kalshi; Louisiana's attorney general sues Kalshi, Polymarket, Robinhood and Coinbase.
deck.storyline: Storyline: prediction markets and their rules · day 3

deck.update: Iran's Guards claim a strike on a US radar in Bahrain after a strike on Sirik; CENTCOM says it shot down two drones and nothing was hit.

alsoToday.headline: US signs voluntary industry guidelines for spyware under the Pall Mall Process
alsoToday.summary: The Pall Mall Process, a UK- and France-led initiative, released voluntary industry guidelines for commercial cyber intrusion capabilities such as spyware, following last year's code for states, and the US signed on, CyberScoop reports. Human rights groups say the guidelines are weaker than they wanted; how AI changes the market was a key topic.
alsoToday.whyItMatters: Voluntary rules with no reporting mechanism yet; watch whether governments tie procurement to them.

alsoToday.headline: Nigeria ends Ebola contact monitoring with no further cases
alsoToday.summary: Nigeria's disease agency says all 62 contacts of its first Ebola patient in more than a decade, a Swiss woman who had travelled from Uganda, completed 21 days of monitoring without falling ill. Al Jazeera notes the separate outbreak in DR Congo has killed more than 5,300 people.
alsoToday.whyItMatters: Contained in Nigeria; the Congo outbreak remains the regional risk.

alsoToday.headline: OpenAI board member Paul Christiano warns of a near-term AI takeover risk
alsoToday.summary: Paul Christiano, an OpenAI Foundation board member and head of the Alignment Research Center, said in a Toronto lecture that if AI follows "the most rapid trajectory" humanity faces "something like a coin flip of an AI takeover", including a meaningful risk in the next six to 12 months, Ars Technica reports.
alsoToday.whyItMatters: A board member of the world's best-known AI lab now says this publicly, days after Anthropic said AI is accelerating its own research. Expect it to feature in the lawsuits and hearings already under way.
alsoToday.storyline: Storyline: warnings about AI risk · day 1
alsoToday.detailHtml: Paul Christiano, an OpenAI Foundation board member and head of the Alignment Research Center, said in a Toronto lecture that if AI follows "the most rapid trajectory" humanity faces "something like a coin flip of an AI takeover", including a meaningful risk in the next six to 12 months, Ars Technica reports. He said the risk stays "exceptionally high" even with realistic policy responses.

alsoToday.headline: Talanx posts record nine months as large losses run EUR 750M under budget
alsoToday.summary: Talanx, the group behind HDI and Hannover Re, reported record nine-month group net income of EUR 2.195bn, up 12%, with large losses about EUR 750M below budget, Insurance Business reports. Insurance Business also says the Microsoft 365 outage has put cloud concentration risk back on brokers' agendas.
alsoToday.whyItMatters: A second large European (re)insurer after Munich Re reporting a benign catastrophe year; that supports softer reinsurance pricing at the January renewals.

alsoToday.headline: Svitolina stuns Sabalenka to reach the WTA Finals semi-finals
alsoToday.summary: Elina Svitolina beat Aryna Sabalenka in three sets, breaking her serve six times, to reach the WTA Finals semi-finals, where she plays Linda Noskova; Mirra Andreeva meets Jessica Pegula, Reuters reports.
alsoToday.whyItMatters: The season-ending title is now open.

alsoToday.headline: Bethesda confirms Fallout 5 and remasters of Fallout 3 and New Vegas
alsoToday.summary: Bethesda has officially announced Fallout 5, currently in pre-production, along with remasters of Fallout 3 and Fallout: New Vegas for modern platforms, Polygon reports, a day after Xbox revealed Wolfenstein 3.
alsoToday.whyItMatters: Microsoft is leaning on its biggest game franchises as Xbox turns 25.

alsoToday.headline: Paraguay widens charges against ex-president Peña over Ueno Bank's collapse
alsoToday.summary: Prosecutors confirmed Ueno Bank-linked assets abroad and are seeking wider charges against impeached president Santiago Peña, who is in pre-trial detention and accused of using his office to benefit the digital bank, AFP reports. The central bank says 1.8 million depositors have had money back from the guarantee fund, though Ueno claimed 2.9 million customers and much of its money is still…
alsoToday.whyItMatters: A digital bank that held deposits for nearly half the country, and government funds, shows what concentration and political ties can do; regulators elsewhere will cite it.
alsoToday.update: Prosecutors seek wider charges against ousted president Peña and confirm Ueno assets abroad; 1.8M depositors partly repaid.
alsoToday.storyline: Storyline: when digital banks fail · day 2
alsoToday.detailHtml: Prosecutors confirmed Ueno Bank-linked assets abroad and are seeking wider charges against impeached president Santiago Peña, who is in pre-trial detention and accused of using his office to benefit the digital bank, AFP reports. The central bank says 1.8 million depositors have had money back from the guarantee fund, though Ueno claimed 2.9 million customers and much of its money is still missing; 27 executives face charges.
